provenance.instrument: Worcester Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 150 Zoning, adopted by the Board of Supervisors 4-11-1988 by Ord. No. 100, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WO1349, Township of Worcester, Montgomery County (150-227 sends appeals to the Court of Common Pleas of Montgomery County, 150-110.3F(7) names the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds). The accessory dwelling units are part of the Conservation Subdivisions article (Article XVIA, Ord. No. 153 of 1997 and Ord. No. 208 of 2006). District uses and figures are text in each article. The only attachment is the table of zoning map amendments. Floodplain rules are in the zoning chapter (Article XX). New Laws: Ord. No. 257 (sewers), No. 304 (stormwater) and No. 305 (Planning Commission and subdivision), none on zoning
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 08-20-2025.' New Laws: Ord. No. 257 (2016, sewers), Ord. No. 304 (8-19-2026, stormwater), Ord. No. 305 (10-21-2026, Planning Commission and subdivision). None amends Chapter 150
checks: Accessory dwelling units are allowed only in a conservation subdivision under Option 3, country properties, in the AGR district: 'Up to two accessory dwelling units shall also be permitted in Option 3' (150-110.2A(1)(c)). In AGR, single-family homes on tracts of eight acres or more are developed under Article XVIA (150-11B(2)). Option 3 allows one principal dwelling per 10 acres of gross tract (150-110.3C, 150-110.4C)

A single-family detached dwelling on a lot in a conservation subdivision under 150-110.3C 'shall also include the concept of accessory dwellings if permitted by that section' (150-9 'Single-family detached dwelling')

One ADU on a lot of at least five but less than 10 acres. Up to two on a lot of 10 acres or more. One may have up to 1,200 sq ft of gross floor area, the other up to 950 sq ft. An existing historic accessory building more than 75 years old may be used even if larger, and need not meet the 150-110.6 setbacks (150-110.3C(2), (3))

The ADU is 'located within the principal dwelling unit or in existing or new outbuildings (such as barns, stables, carriage houses, garages, and spring houses)' and must harmonize with the house. No part may be more than 500 ft from the house, except an existing historic accessory building. The ADU may not have its own accessory building such as a garage (150-110.3C(1), (4), (5))

But 150-177A(10) says 'Dwelling units are expressly prohibited within any permitted accessory structure', and since 2021 accessory uses in conservation subdivisions must comply with Article XXIV (150-110.2A(3)). Whether an ADU in an outbuilding is still allowed is not settled

Before a building permit (or a use and occupancy permit for an existing building) the owner must record a restrictive covenant against enlarging the ADU, and the Montgomery County Health Department must approve the sewage system (150-110.3C(6))

A 10-acre tract existing on 1-1-2006 may have up to two ADUs 'in conformance with § 150-110.20C', with a deed restriction against further dwelling units (150-110.4C(2)(a)). 150-110.20 is reserved, so the cross-reference leads nowhere

Option 3 lots: at least 60,000 sq ft, 300 ft wide at the building line, yards of 100 ft. Impervious cover by lot size, for example 12% at 5 to 5.99 acres and 6% at 9 to 13.99 acres. Height 35 ft, 2.5 stories. New dwellings stand 100 ft from external roads and 50 ft from other tract boundaries (150-110.6 to 150-110.9)

Accessory structures to a house stand only in the rear or side yard. Over 250 and under 1,200 sq ft: 15 ft from the side and rear lines and 20 ft tall at most. 1,200 to under 3,000 sq ft: 20 ft and 25 ft (150-177A(1))
Parking: 'Two all-weather parking spaces per family' for a dwelling (150-153A)
'No dwelling shall be constructed unless the same shall have an inhabitable floor area of at least 900 square feet' (150-183). Whether it reaches an ADU is not settled

Every district's use list ends 'and no other' (for example 150-11, 150-19, 150-83), so a use not listed is not allowed. R-AG-175, R-175, R-150, R-100 and R-75 allow agriculture, one single-family detached dwelling and accessory uses

Floodplain Conservation District (Article XX): 'No new construction, alteration, or improvement of buildings and any other type of permanent structure' (150-138B(1)). Existing structures may be enlarged only within the flood elevation limits and not toward the stream, and no new construction within 50 ft of a top of bank without a variance (150-138C, D)

Riparian Corridor Conservation District (at least 75 ft from a waterway, or the 100-year floodplain): no buildings, and existing nonconforming buildings in it may not be enlarged (150-146.6, 150-146.8A, 150-146.9A)
Lots approved before 4-11-1988 may be built on despite their area or width, with the district yards (150-173). An expansion of a nonconforming structure must meet the district rules (150-162.1)
Variances: 150-217C, 150-219. No bar on a use variance
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Worcester Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Article IV (AGR), Article V (R-AG-200), Article XIII (MR), Article XVIA (Conservation Subdivisions), 150-138, Article XXB, Article XXIII, 150-153, 150-173, 150-177, 150-183, Article XXVI, the 150-9 definitions of single-family detached dwelling and dwelling types, the New Laws page and code searches (ADU terms, conservation subdivision, single-family and two-family, multifamily and conversion). The use lists of R-AG-175 (150-27), R-175 (150-35), R-150 (150-51), R-100 (150-67), R-75 (150-75) and RO (150-91) were read only in search results. Not read: Articles I to III except those definitions, the R-AG-175 to R-75 and RO articles in full, MHD, R-50, LPD (Article XVIB), C, SC, LI, IR, the SS, AQRC, Cedars Village and Billboard overlays, Article XXI signs, the rest of Articles XX, XXII and XXIV, Article XXV, XXVII to XXX. The code search for ADU terms finds them only in Article XVIA.

term.note: 'Up to two accessory dwelling units are permitted on a lot, incidental to the primary permitted use and not conducted as an independent principal use'

status.note: Option 3 country properties are permitted by right on tracts of eight acres or more in AGR, with up to two ADUs on a lot

scope_districts.note: In AGR, single-family homes on tracts of eight acres or more follow Article XVIA, Conservation Subdivisions

status_outside.note: The other district use lists do not name an accessory dwelling unit and end 'and no other'. 150-177A(10) bars dwelling units in any accessory structure

path.note: 'On tracts eight acres or larger, the following three conservation subdivision options are permitted by right.' A conservation subdivision also follows the four-step design process and subdivision approval under Chapter 130 (150-110.9A)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board, on the usual findings. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Multifamily dwelling in a development (MR)
value.conditions: 'Multifamily dwelling in accordance with the regulations in this article' (150-83B). A multifamily dwelling is 'A building consisting of two or more dwelling units' separated by party walls (150-9). Five acres for every development, 300 ft wide, four units an acre of developable area for multifamily types other than apartment houses, a single plan and architectural scheme, 75 ft buffers (150-84, 150-89E). Two spaces per dwelling unit (150-88A)
value.note: A planned development of two or more units, not a unit added to a house

historic_bypass.note: No historic ADU path. An existing historic accessory building over 75 years old has its own size and setback exemption (150-110.3C(3))

building_types.note: Option 3 country properties are single-family detached dwellings

value.condition: An ADU is allowed only on a lot in a conservation subdivision under Option 3, country properties: a tract of eight acres or more in AGR, with one principal dwelling per 10 acres of gross tract, and lots restricted from further subdivision.
One ADU needs a lot of at least five acres, and two need 10 acres

An Option 3 lot follows the conservation subdivision figures: at least 60,000 sq ft, 300 ft wide at the building line, front, side and rear yards of 100 ft, impervious cover by lot size (12% at 5 to 5.99 acres, 6% at 9 to 13.99 acres), and new dwellings 100 ft from external roads and 50 ft from other tract boundaries.

The ADU must harmonize with the house. No part of it may be more than 500 ft from the house, except an existing historic accessory building, and the ADU may not have its own accessory building such as a garage.
Before the permit, the owner records a restrictive covenant against enlarging the ADU, and the Montgomery County Health Department approves the sewage system.
In the Floodplain Conservation District, no new construction of buildings and no other permanent structure is permitted.

In the Floodplain Conservation District the code bars 'alteration, or improvement of buildings'. Improvements to an existing structure follow 150-138D: work of 50% or more of its market value is a substantial improvement that must fully comply.

In the Riparian Corridor Conservation District (at least 75 ft from an identified waterway, or the 100-year floodplain) no building or other permanent structure is permitted, and an existing nonconforming building may not be enlarged.

districts_in_doubt.note: R-AG-200 permits a single-family detached dwelling 'In accordance with the regulations and requirements of Article IV (AGR Agricultural District)'. Whether that brings in the AGR route to an Option 3 conservation subdivision with ADUs is not settled

districts_read_no_listing.note: MR permits the underlying district's uses and multifamily dwellings. Its own list names no ADU

types_in_conflict.note: 150-110.3C(1) allows an ADU 'in existing or new outbuildings (such as barns, stables, carriage houses, garages, and spring houses)'. 150-177A(10) says 'Dwelling units are expressly prohibited within any permitted accessory structure', and 150-110.2A(3) (Ord. No. 284, 2021) makes accessory uses in conservation subdivisions comply with Article XXIV

types_not_addressed.note: The section names a unit within the house or in an outbuilding, not an addition

max_sqft.note: 'The gross floor area of one accessory dwelling unit shall not exceed 1,200 square feet. The gross floor area of the other accessory dwelling unit, where permitted, shall not exceed 950 square feet.'

value.what: an existing historic accessory building more than 75 years old

exempt_building.note: 'existing historic accessory buildings more than 75 years old exceeding these floor area limits may be permitted to be used as an accessory dwelling unit, and shall not be required to meet the setback requirements set forth in § 150-110.6'

internal_uses_district_height.note: Principal building: 35 ft, not exceeding 2.5 stories. The accessory building height subsection of 150-110.8 was repealed in 2021

front_yard_barred.note: Accessory structures to a single-family home 'shall be located in the rear yard or side yard only'

value.where: An accessory structure over 250 and under 1,200 sq ft of gross floor area
An accessory structure of 1,200 sq ft to under 3,000 sq ft of gross floor area

accessory_rules_where.note: Accessory structures of 250 sq ft or less: 10 ft and 12 ft

max_adus.note: One on a lot of five to under 10 acres, up to two on 10 acres or more

max_adus_by_lot_size.note: 'On lots less than 10 acres but at least five acres in area, a maximum of one accessory dwelling unit is permitted. On lots 10 acres or larger, up to two accessory dwelling units are permitted.'

spaces_required.note: 'Dwelling. Two all-weather parking spaces per family'

reading.value: The code asks two spaces per family for a dwelling. If the ADU household counts as a family, it needs two more spaces, four in all with the house

min_lot_sqft.note: For a lot outside a conservation subdivision. Option 3 lots: 60,000 sq ft (150-110.6). Width 250 ft

setback_front_ft.note: 75 ft from local and secondary feeder streets, 100 ft from collector, primary and scenic roads, measured from the ultimate right-of-way

setback_side_ft.note: 'Fifty feet shall be the minimum size of each of two side yards'

max_building_coverage.note: 'Ten percent shall be the maximum total building coverage at each lot.'
